REASONING:
Step 1 – Frame the project  
- **Objective:** Expand coverage of the Digital Civil and Social Identifier (DCSID) and strengthen inclusion of the National Population Registry (NPR) and Social Registry (SR) – especially in rural/remote areas – to improve targeting and access to social‑protection programmes.  
- **Scope & Components:** 1) Strengthen/extend NPR and operationalise the National Registry Agency (NRA); 2) Expand and enhance the SR system; 3) Project Management, Capacity Building and M&E.  
- **Delivery model:** Implemented by the Ministry of Interior (MoI) through a Project Management Unit (PMU) and an Inter‑ministerial Steering Committee (IMSC), with World Bank technical and supervisory support, under Performance‑Based Conditions (PBCs).  
- **Timeline:** Expected approval 04‑Dec‑2024; closing 31‑Dec‑2028.  
- **Budget:** US $70 million (EUR 62.6 million).  
- **Key stakeholders:** Borrower (Kingdom of Morocco), MoI (implementing agency), PMU, IMSC, World Bank, EU (communication support), CNSS, other ministries (MEF, HCP).  
- **External dependencies:** Legal framework (Law 72‑18, decrees, Law 09‑08 on data protection), civil‑registry offices, biometric solution providers, satellite/mobile‑unit connectivity, climate‑related shocks.

Step 2 – Category sweep (candidate risks with supporting evidence)  

| Category | Candidate risk | Evidence (≤25 words) |
|----------|----------------|----------------------|
| technical | Legacy data inconsistencies may cause inaccurate enrolment/exclusions. | “existing databases had inconsistent quality and data formats, including Arabic and Latin alphabets, likely leading to substantial inaccuracies and processing requirements.” |
| technical | Remote‑area ICT infrastructure may be insufficient. | “some of the 2,200 Civil Registry Offices are in very isolated areas and require substantial investments in overall infrastructure, beyond new hardware and software.” |
| technical | Data‑privacy breach despite privacy‑by‑design. | “MoI adopted a privacy‑by‑design approach to guarantee data privacy and protection.” |
| technical | EFC monitoring system may be ineffective. | “design and development of an end‑to‑end Error, Fraud, and Corruption (EFC) monitoring system and mitigation strategy to reduce its rate.” |
| organizational | Transition of NPR/SR management to the newly created NRA may stall. | “Implementation of the NPR and the SR will be managed by the DIST … until the NRA is operational.” |
| financial | Use of Excel for IFRs may affect quality/timeliness. | “use of a spreadsheet ‘Excel’ … may lead to challenges in quality and timeliness of IFRs and annual financial statements.” |
| financial | Duplicate budgeting (e.g., AMO‑TADAMON) could cause reporting errors. | “risk of duplication or overlap due to the use of the same budget line ‘AMO‑TADAMON’ to justify expenditure.” |
| financial | Retroactive financing limited to 12‑month‑old expenditures – cash‑flow risk. | “Retroactive financing may only be provided … for eligible expenditures incurred not more than 12 months before signing.” |
| schedule | NRA operationalisation and staff recruitment may be delayed (PBCs). | “PBCs target NRA operationalisation and staff recruitment by FY26 (see Table 2).” |
| schedule | NPR coverage target (≥60 % by 2028) may slip. | “The NPR national rollout strategy aims to expand coverage to more than 60 percent of the total population by end of 2024.” |
| stakeholder | Informal‑sector workers may avoid enrolment fearing taxation. | “workers in the informal sector are wary of providing their information … due to perceived risks of making them susceptible to taxation.” |
| stakeholder | Vulnerable groups could be excluded due to poor communication. | “Potential negative social impacts … mainly related to the exclusion of some vulnerable groups due to inefficient or inadequate public communication and outreach efforts.” |
| political_regulatory | Changes to Law 72‑18 or its decrees could affect implementation. | “Law no. 72‑18 and the three implementing decrees provide a solid legal and institutional framework.” |
| political_regulatory | Amendments to data‑protection law (Law 09‑08) could create compliance gaps. | “The project will follow national regulations related to personal data protection (Law 09‑08).” |
| environmental | Mobile units/e‑waste may be improperly disposed. | “Risks associated with the use of electronic devices (such as mobile units) include the potential generation of e‑waste and its improper disposal.” |
| external | Climate‑related shocks (drought, floods) may increase demand on social protection. | “Morocco has undergone several overlapping shocks … climate change … droughts … represent significant risks to the Moroccan economy.” |
| external | Economic recession from COVID‑19 could affect funding/beneficiary ability. | “The COVID‑19 pandemic led to the first recession in over two decades due to reduced economic activity.” |

Step 3 – Evidence filter  
All candidate risks are directly supported by statements in the appraisal document; none are discarded.

Step 4 – Assess & Mitigate  

| Risk ID | Likelihood (1‑5) | Impact (1‑5) | Justification | Mitigation |
|---------|------------------|--------------|---------------|------------|
| R01 | 4 | 4 | Legacy data quality is known to be poor; errors would undermine targeting. | Conduct comprehensive data cleaning, validation and biometric deduplication before enrolment; institute ongoing quality‑control checks. |
| R02 | 3 | 3 | Remote offices need extra infrastructure; failures would delay enrolment. | Provide backup power, satellite links, and a maintenance schedule; pre‑position spare equipment. |
| R03 | 2 | 5 | Breach would damage trust and violate law; impact is severe. | Implement strong encryption, regular security audits, and staff training; monitor compliance with Law 09‑08. |
| R04 | 3 | 4 | Fraud detection is critical; an ineffective system could cause leakages. | Engage experienced anti‑fraud vendor, pilot the EFC system, and refine based on monitoring results. |
| R05 | 3 | 4 | Institutional hand‑over is complex; delays affect whole project. | Develop a detailed hand‑over plan, recruit NRA staff early, and provide capacity‑building workshops. |
| R06 | 3 | 4 | Spreadsheet‑based reporting risks inaccurate financial statements. | Adopt dedicated financial management software, automate IFR generation, and train FM staff. |
| R07 | 2 | 3 | Duplicate budget lines could cause audit findings. | Enforce strict budget‑coding procedures and cross‑check with World Bank templates. |
| R08 | 2 | 3 | Retroactive financing limits cash availability for early activities. | Maintain a cash‑flow buffer and align expenditures with eligible‑expenditure windows. |
| R09 | 3 | 4 | NRA operational milestones are PBC‑linked; delay stalls downstream activities. | Set monthly milestone tracking, early recruitment, and regular IMSC reviews. |
| R10 | 3 | 3 | Achieving 60 % coverage may be slower than planned. | Intensify enrolment campaigns, monitor weekly enrolment rates, and deploy additional mobile units as needed. |
| R11 | 3 | 3 | Informal workers’ reluctance reduces coverage of the poorest. | Tailor outreach, assure no tax penalties, and simplify enrolment procedures. |
| R12 | 3 | 3 | Poor communication can leave vulnerable groups out. | Deploy multi‑channel communication (TV, radio, SMS, community agents) and conduct feedback loops. |
| R13 | 2 | 3 | Legal amendments could stall activities. | Establish a legal‑monitoring unit and maintain dialogue with the Ministry of Justice. |
| R14 | 2 | 3 | Data‑protection law changes could create compliance gaps. | Periodic review of Law 09‑08, update privacy‑by‑design controls accordingly. |
| R15 | 2 | 2 | E‑waste is a minor but manageable environmental risk. | Adopt certified e‑waste recycling procedures and include disposal clauses in procurement. |
| R16 | 4 | 4 | Climate shocks can dramatically increase beneficiary numbers. | Build flexible targeting algorithms and reserve contingency funds for emergency responses. |
| R17 | 3 | 3 | Economic downturn may affect government fiscal space. | Diversify financing sources and maintain a contingency reserve within the loan. |

Step 5 – Consolidate  
All identified risks are distinct and supported by evidence; the register contains 17 risks.
